questions.q: Chief Okafor wants written evidence that he owns 1,500 shares in a company quoted on the Nigerian Exchange. Which document should he obtain?
questions.explanation: A share certificate is issued to a shareholder as evidence of ownership of the number of shares stated on it. A prospectus only invites the public to subscribe to securities, while a share transfer form is used when ownership is being transferred.

questions.q: A company in Lagos issues new ordinary shares to the public for the first time through the Nigerian Exchange. The market in which this transaction takes place is called the
questions.explanation: New securities are first issued and sold in the primary market, which enables the company to raise fresh capital. The secondary market deals in the buying and selling of existing securities among investors.

questions.q: An investor in Ibadan needs cash urgently and sells his shares of a quoted bank on the Nigerian Exchange instead of waiting for the company to buy them back. The stock exchange is performing the function of
options: providing a market for existing securities
guaranteeing a fixed return to shareholders
questions.explanation: The investor is able to sell existing shares to another investor, showing that the stock exchange provides a market for existing securities. Raising fresh capital relates to new issues, and the stock exchange does not guarantee returns to shareholders.

questions.q: A beverage manufacturer in Ibadan places large illuminated boards along the Lagos–Ibadan expressway to remind travellers about its products. This advertising medium is most suitable because it
options: reaches many road users repeatedly at relatively low cost per viewer
is best for giving detailed technical information
ensures that only interested buyers see the message
allows immediate two-way communication with customers
questions.explanation: Billboards expose an advertising message to many travellers and can be seen repeatedly over a period. They do not allow two-way communication or detailed explanation, and they are seen by many people who may not be interested buyers.

questions.q: A bottling company in Onitsha sponsors a community football tournament and donates water to flood victims. This activity is best classified as
questions.explanation: Sponsorship and donations are used to create goodwill and a favourable image for the company, which is public relations. Personal selling involves direct persuasion by a salesperson, while sales promotion usually offers short-term incentives to stimulate purchases.

questions.q: A customer in Jos buys a sealed bottle of fruit juice from a supermarket and finds a piece of plastic inside it. Which consumer right is most directly threatened?
questions.explanation: The right to safety protects consumers from goods that may endanger their health or life. A foreign object in a drink is a direct danger to health, while the other rights relate more to choice, knowledge and presenting complaints.

questions.q: Which Nigerian agency is primarily responsible for controlling the manufacture, importation and sale of packaged food and drugs to ensure they are safe and properly labelled?
options: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC)
questions.explanation: NAFDAC regulates food, drugs, cosmetics and similar products to ensure they are safe, effective and properly labelled. SON sets product standards, the FCCPC handles competition and consumer complaints, and the Customs Service is mainly concerned with border control and duties.

questions.q: A trader in Kano receives a document from a supplier stating the prices of goods and the terms on which the supplier is willing to sell, before the trader places an order. The document is a
questions.explanation: A quotation is sent in response to an enquiry, giving prices and terms before an order is placed. A proforma invoice is a provisional invoice for goods to be supplied, a delivery note accompanies goods, and a credit note corrects an overcharge.

questions.q: An exporter in Kano sends fresh flowers by air to a buyer in London. Which document is issued by the airline as an acknowledgement that the goods have been received for carriage?
questions.explanation: The air waybill is the contract of carriage and receipt for goods sent by air. A bill of lading is used for sea shipment, a consignment note is commonly used for road or rail transport, and a certificate of origin shows the country where goods were produced.

questions.q: Bola, a retailer in Surulere, receives a document from a wholesaler which states the quantity, description and price of goods supplied and shows the total amount payable. The document is a/an
questions.explanation: An invoice gives details of the goods supplied and the total amount due for payment. A credit note is issued for returned goods or overcharges, while a statement of account summarises transactions over a period.

questions.q: Mrs. Adeyemi buys a generating set from a dealer in Ikeja by paying ₦80,000 as deposit and agreeing to pay the balance in ten monthly instalments. The generating set remains the property of the dealer until the last instalment is paid. This transaction is an example of
questions.explanation: Hire purchase involves payment by deposit and instalments, with ownership passing only after the final payment. In a credit sale, the buyer may pay later, but ownership normally passes immediately.

questions.q: Chika buys 500 bags of rice from a mill in Abakaliki and sells them in lots of 20 bags to retailers in Enugu. The wholesaler is performing the function of
questions.explanation: Breaking bulk means buying goods in large quantities and selling them in smaller quantities to retailers. Risk bearing and financing retailers would require evidence of loss-sharing or credit facilities, which are not shown here.

questions.q: A Nigerian exporter in Lagos draws a bill of exchange on an importer in London. A bank in London accepts the bill. The main effect of the bank's acceptance is that the exporter is assured of
questions.explanation: Acceptance of a bill by a bank means the bank promises to pay the bill when it matures. It does not affect delivery time, customs duty liability or freight charges.

questions.q: In a year, Nigeria's visible imports are ₦9.6 trillion while visible exports are ₦7.2 trillion. This means the country has
options: an adverse balance of trade of ₦2.4 trillion
a favourable balance of trade of ₦2.4 trillion
an adverse balance of payments of ₦16.8 trillion
a balanced balance of trade of ₦2.4 trillion
questions.explanation: The visible trade balance is ₦9.6 trillion minus ₦7.2 trillion, giving ₦2.4 trillion. Since imports exceed exports, the balance of trade is adverse by ₦2.4 trillion.

questions.q: Production is said to be complete only when
options: raw materials are extracted from the soil
goods are stored in a warehouse
goods and services reach the final consumer
manufactured goods leave the factory gate
questions.explanation: Production is not complete until goods and services satisfy the wants of the final consumer. Extraction, storage and leaving the factory are stages along the way, not the end of production.

questions.q: One major advantage of using containers in sea transport is that they
options: make ships travel faster than aircraft
reduce handling costs and the risk of pilferage
remove all customs checks on imports
questions.explanation: Containers allow goods to be handled mechanically and kept enclosed, reducing handling costs and theft. They do not remove the need for ports, customs checks, or make ships faster than aircraft.

questions.q: Which mode of transport is most suitable for delivering small consignments of goods door-to-door over short distances within a city?
questions.explanation: Road transport is flexible and can provide direct door-to-door delivery over short distances. Rail and sea transport require terminals, while pipelines are suitable mainly for fluids and gases.

questions.q: Chief Okafor insured the same warehouse against fire with two insurers, one for ₦6,000,000 and the other for ₦9,000,000. A fire caused damage of ₦5,000,000. Under the principle of contribution, how much should the insurer with the ₦6,000,000 policy pay?
questions.explanation: Total cover is ₦15,000,000, so the ₦6,000,000 insurer bears 6/15 of the ₦5,000,000 loss: (6/15) × ₦5,000,000 = ₦2,000,000. The other insurer pays the remaining ₦3,000,000, and contribution prevents the insured from recovering more than the actual loss.

questions.q: Musa, a trader in Kano, insured his shop against fire. During a fire outbreak, part of his building fell and injured a customer. Which insurance covers Musa's legal liability for the customer's injury?
questions.explanation: Public liability insurance covers claims arising from injury or damage suffered by members of the public on the insured's premises. Fire insurance mainly covers damage to insured property, while employer's liability covers employees and fidelity guarantee covers dishonesty of employees.

questions.q: After paying premiums on a life assurance policy for eight years, Mrs. Nwosu decides to terminate the policy before maturity. The amount the insurer pays her is known as the
questions.explanation: A surrender value is the cash amount paid by an insurer when a life assurance policy is terminated before maturity. The sum assured is normally paid on maturity or death, while a bonus is an addition to the policy's benefits.

questions.q: Commercial banks create credit mainly by
options: selling foreign exchange at the official rate
granting loans and advances to customers
questions.explanation: When commercial banks grant loans and advances, they credit customers' accounts, thereby increasing deposits and the volume of money in circulation. Printing currency is a function of the Central Bank of Nigeria, not commercial banks.

questions.q: A public limited company in Lagos wishes to raise capital from the general public by issuing shares. Which document must it publish to invite the public to subscribe to the shares?
questions.explanation: A prospectus is the document that invites the public to subscribe for shares in a company and provides details of the issue. The memorandum sets out the company's relationship with the outside world, while the articles contain internal rules.

questions.q: A shareholder in a quoted Nigerian company wants to sell some of her shares but does not know the current market price. Which facility of the stock exchange most directly enables her to sell the shares at a price determined by market forces?
options: An organised secondary market where securities are bought and sold through authorised stockbrokers
A central bank window for discounting Treasury bills
A company register for issuing new shares directly to the public
A commercial bank counter for converting shares into fixed deposits
questions.explanation: The stock exchange provides a secondary market where existing shares are traded through authorised stockbrokers, and prices are influenced by demand and supply. The other facilities relate to money-market instruments, new share issues, or bank deposits rather than the sale of existing shares at a market price.

questions.q: A retired civil servant in Jos wants to invest in a company's shares that normally receive a fixed rate of dividend before ordinary shareholders are paid. Which class of shares should he buy?
questions.explanation: Preference shares normally carry a fixed rate of dividend and rank ahead of ordinary shares for dividend payment. Ordinary shares receive variable dividends after preference shareholders, while debenture stock is a loan that earns interest rather than a share dividend.

questions.q: A manufacturer of sachet water in Ibadan uses radio announcements to reach thousands of listeners at the same time. Which advantage of advertising over personal selling does this example best illustrate?
options: It is always cheaper than producing the goods advertised
It allows the seller to receive immediate feedback from each buyer
It enables the salesperson to answer individual objections on the spot
It can reach a large number of widely scattered buyers at a relatively low cost per contact
questions.explanation: Radio advertising can communicate with many potential buyers simultaneously, giving it a low cost per contact compared with personal selling. Personal selling is better for immediate feedback and handling individual objections, while advertising is not guaranteed to be cheaper than production.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes marketing from selling?
options: Marketing is used only for consumer goods, while selling is used only for industrial goods
Marketing ends when goods enter the warehouse, while selling begins after the customer has paid
Marketing is concerned only with advertising, while selling covers all forms of transport
Marketing begins by identifying customer needs and then produces goods to satisfy them, while selling focuses mainly on persuading buyers to purchase what has already been produced
questions.explanation: Marketing is customer-centred and starts with identifying needs before production and distribution decisions are made. Selling is narrower and mainly involves persuading buyers to take goods that have already been produced; it is not limited to transport, a type of good, or the moment after payment.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) in Nigeria?
options: To issue Nigerian currency and control inflation
To protect consumers from unfair trade practices and promote fair competition in markets
To regulate the operations of the Nigerian Exchange
To fix the prices of all goods and services in the country
questions.explanation: The FCCPC is charged with consumer protection and the promotion of competition by checking unfair trade practices and abuses in markets. Currency issuance and inflation control are central-bank functions, stock exchange regulation is handled by securities regulators, and general price fixing is not its main role.

questions.q: A wholesaler in Onitsha supplies 15 cartons of soap to a supermarket in Asaba and leaves a document showing the description, quantity, unit price, total amount payable and terms of payment. This document is most likely a (an)
questions.explanation: An invoice gives details of goods supplied, including quantity, unit price, total amount payable and payment terms. A credit note corrects an overcharge or records returned goods, a statement of account summarises transactions over a period, and a bill of lading is a sea-carriage document.

questions.q: A trader in Minna asks a foodstuff supplier in Kaduna to send a document quoting the price and total amount to be paid for 50 bags of garri before the goods are despatched. Which document is most suitable?
questions.explanation: A pro-forma invoice is sent before goods are supplied to show the description, price and total amount payable, often so the buyer can arrange payment. A consignment note accompanies goods in transit, a debit note demands an additional payment, and a bill of exchange orders a debtor to pay.

questions.q: A wholesaler in Kano buys 600 cartons of milk from a manufacturer and sells them in lots of 30 cartons to retailers. The function performed by the wholesaler is called
questions.explanation: Breaking bulk means dividing large consignments bought from producers into smaller quantities for retailers. Warehousing and financing are other wholesaler functions, but they are not shown by the act of selling 600 cartons in lots of 30.

questions.q: A wholesaler in Ibadan bought 200 bags of rice at ₦28,000 per bag. He sold 150 bags at ₦32,000 each and the remaining 50 bags at ₦30,000 each. What was his total profit?
Which of the following is a service commonly rendered by a retailer to a wholesaler?
options: Supplying information about consumers' preferences and demand
questions.explanation: Retailers are in direct contact with final consumers, so they can pass useful information on tastes and demand back to wholesalers. Breaking bulk is mainly a wholesaler's service, while manufacturing and long-term lending to producers are not usual retailing functions.

questions.q: An exporter in Port Harcourt issues a bill of exchange ordering an importer in Abidjan to pay a stated sum. The exporter, who issues the order to pay, is called the
questions.explanation: The drawer is the party that draws or issues the bill and orders another party to pay. The drawee is the party ordered to pay, while an endorser transfers a bill already issued.

questions.q: A printing firm in Ibadan buys ink and paper which are used up in producing pamphlets during one production period. These items are examples of
questions.explanation: Circulating capital consists of materials and inputs that are used up within a production cycle, such as ink and paper. Fixed capital, such as a printing machine, is used repeatedly over several production periods.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a tertiary occupation?
questions.explanation: Tertiary occupations provide services rather than extract or manufacture goods; insurance brokerage is a service occupation. Tin mining and fishing are primary occupations, while blacksmithing is a secondary occupation.

questions.q: Chief Okeke starts a rice-milling business in Abakaliki using his savings and borrowed funds. Which of the following best describes his role as an entrepreneur?
options: Providing only labour in the production process
Coordinating other factors of production and bearing the risk of the business
Receiving fixed interest on capital lent to the firm
questions.explanation: An entrepreneur organises land, labour and capital and bears the risk of loss or profit in the business. Supplying land earns rent, lending capital earns interest, and providing labour earns wages, so those roles belong to other factor owners.

questions.q: A shipping service that does not operate on fixed routes or sailing schedules but moves wherever cargo is available is called a
questions.explanation: Tramp ships are chartered according to available cargo and move from port to port without fixed schedules. Liner services, by contrast, operate on advertised routes and regular sailing dates.

questions.q: A businesswoman in Sokoto wants to send a written message electronically from her computer to a supplier in Lagos through the internet. The service she should use is
questions.explanation: Electronic mail sends written messages from one computer to another over the internet. Telex is an older telegraphic system, fax sends document copies over telephone lines, and courier service carries physical packages.

questions.q: Shortly after receiving a fire insurance proposal from Mrs. Ngozi in Aba, an insurer issues a temporary document confirming that the risk is covered until the full policy is prepared. This temporary document is called a
questions.explanation: A cover note is issued by an insurer as temporary evidence that insurance cover has commenced before the main policy document is ready. A proposal form is only an application for insurance, while a premium receipt merely acknowledges payment and does not itself confirm the terms of cover.

questions.q: A policyholder in Jos has paid premiums on a life assurance policy for several years but can no longer continue paying. The policy may remain in force for a reduced sum assured. This arrangement is known as
questions.explanation: A paid-up policy arises when premiums stop after a period and the policy remains in force, usually for a reduced sum assured. A surrender value is the cash amount paid if the policyholder decides to terminate the policy before maturity.

questions.q: A motorist in Port Harcourt sells his insured car and, with the insurer's consent, transfers his interest in the insurance policy to the buyer. This transfer is called
questions.explanation: Assignment is the transfer of the rights and interest in an insurance policy from one person to another. Subrogation occurs when the insurer takes over the insured person's right to recover losses from a third party after paying a claim.

questions.q: Which bank account is most suitable for a trader in Ibadan who wants to keep money for a fixed period in order to earn a higher rate of interest?
questions.explanation: A fixed deposit account is designed for money left with the bank for an agreed period, and it usually attracts a higher rate of interest than a savings account. A current account is mainly for day-to-day transactions and normally earns little or no interest.

questions.q: A document prepared by a bank showing all payments into and withdrawals from a customer's account over a period is called a
questions.explanation: A bank statement records the transactions on a customer's account, including deposits and withdrawals, over a stated period. A bank draft is a payment instrument, while a cheque book contains forms used to instruct the bank to make payments.

questions.q: An online shop in Enugu sells mobile phones directly to individual customers and delivers the phones to their homes. This type of e-commerce transaction is known as
questions.explanation: Business-to-consumer e-commerce occurs when a business sells goods or services directly to individual final consumers. Consumer-to-consumer e-commerce involves individuals selling to other individuals, often through online marketplaces.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major advantage of e-commerce to a small tailoring business in Lagos?
options: It eliminates all risks of fraud in business transactions.
It removes the need for the owner to keep proper records.
It guarantees that every customer will pay promptly.
It can sell to customers outside its immediate location at a relatively low cost.
questions.explanation: E-commerce allows a small business to display and sell its products online to customers in distant places without the cost of opening many physical shops. It does not remove the need for records, guarantee prompt payment, or eliminate fraud risks.

questions.q: A shareholder holds cumulative preference shares in a company that made no profit and paid no dividend last year. If the company makes profit this year and declares dividend, the shareholder is entitled to
options: an automatic allotment of new ordinary shares in place of the unpaid dividend
the ordinary dividend because preference shareholders rank with ordinary shareholders
only the current year's dividend because unpaid dividends are lost
the arrears of last year's dividend and the current year's dividend before ordinary shareholders are paid
questions.explanation: Cumulative preference shares carry the right to arrears of unpaid dividends before ordinary shareholders are paid in a profitable year. Unpaid preference dividends are not forfeited, and they do not turn automatically into ordinary shares or rank equally with ordinary shareholders.

questions.q: An automobile dealer in Kano advertises that only ten units of a new car model are available at a special price during the week. The main purpose of the advertisement is to
options: build long-term goodwill through community service
remind customers about a product they have used for many years
provide technical details to help buyers compare the model with rivals
create a sense of urgency that encourages immediate purchase
questions.explanation: The limited number of units and the special price for the week are designed to make buyers act quickly for fear of missing the offer. It is not mainly informative, reminder or public relations advertising.

questions.q: Two cement companies meet privately and agree to sell a particular grade of cement at exactly ₦9,000 per bag so that neither undercuts the other. This anti-competitive practice is known as
questions.explanation: Price fixing occurs when competitors agree on the price to charge instead of allowing market competition to determine it. Price discrimination charges different buyers different prices, while resale price maintenance sets resale conditions and hoarding withholds goods from the market.

questions.q: Mrs. Bello in Jos discovers that a pressing iron she bought two days ago is faulty. Which of the following will best strengthen her claim for redress from the seller?
options: Reporting the matter to a competing dealer in the same market
Taking the iron to a different shop for repair before informing the seller
Using the iron continuously to see whether the fault will disappear
Producing the sales receipt and the warranty card
questions.explanation: The sales receipt proves that Mrs. Bello bought the iron from that seller, and the warranty card shows the seller's or manufacturer's repair or replacement obligation. Repairing it elsewhere or continuing to use it may weaken her claim, while reporting to a competitor does not establish her purchase.

questions.q: A Nigerian importer wishes to arrange payment through a letter of credit before a foreign supplier ships the goods. The supplier sends a document showing provisional prices and quantities to enable the importer to obtain the letter of credit. This document is a
questions.explanation: A pro forma invoice is sent before a sale is completed and gives provisional details that the importer can use to arrange a letter of credit. It is not the final commercial invoice demanding payment, nor a transport document or a credit note.
